analysis.investment_thesis: The Oberoi brand is prestigious, but prestige does not protect shareholders paying 4.28x book and 26.5x earnings for a company that posted losses in two of the last five years. Luxury hospitality has high fixed costs, profound cyclicality, and I refuse to pay an asset-light multiple for a very asset-heavy business.
key_strengths: Exceptionally low debt — D/E of just 0.05 with total borrowings of INR 250 Cr against equity of INR 4,706 Cr; the balance sheet is essentially ungeared
Powerful operating recovery: EBITDA grew from -INR 225 Cr (FY21) to INR 1,298 Cr (FY25) — management preserved the asset base through a catastrophic period
Industry-leading operating margins of 38.9% reflect genuine pricing power of the Oberoi brand in luxury hospitality
key_risks: Net losses in FY21 (-INR 375 Cr) and FY22 (-INR 95 Cr) break my requirement for 5 consecutive years of positive earnings — the company has not yet rebuilt its track record
P/B of 4.28x means shareholders are paying four times book for fixed hospitality assets that can be permanently impaired by another pandemic, geopolitical event, or recession
OCF was negative in 2 of the last 5 years — the hotel business is capital-hungry with INR 485 Cr of capex in FY25 alone, and free cash generation remains lumpy
red_flags: P/E of 26.5x and P/B of 4.28x — both materially above my maximum thresholds with no margin of safety
Recent losses in FY21 and FY22 violate the consecutive positive earnings criterion — a fundamental disqualifier in my framework
Rising capex (INR 485 Cr in FY25 vs INR 67 Cr in FY22) signals heavy capital commitment just as investors are paying peak cycle earnings multiples
analysis.detailed_analysis:
EIH Limited (Oberoi Hotels) is a fine enterprise run with prudent financial discipline — the near-zero debt is a genuine virtue I appreciate. But the earnings record disqualifies it under my methodology: losses of INR 375 Cr in FY21 and INR 95 Cr in FY22 mean this company has not demonstrated five consecutive years of uninterrupted positive earning power, which is my baseline requirement. COVID was external, yes — but my framework does not grant exemptions for causes, only outcomes.

The price embeds recovery optimism in full. At 4.28x book value and 26.5x trailing earnings, the market has already paid for the turnaround. The investor buying today at INR 322 receives no discount for the permanent risk of cyclical demand collapse. Hotels are capital-intensive fixed assets; should occupancy fall materially, neither brand nor management skill prevents impairment. I require the stock to trade near or below book value before a hotel company enters my consideration set.
